    Goal¶

    Write a new tabular generator step by step: the GeneratorMixin contract, generate signatures, testing, and benchmark registration.

    Creating a (tabular_data) generator: Scenario¶

    Label noise is a common data-quality defect: some rows carry the wrong class label, and classifiers trained on such data silently degrade.

    The generator here flips a fraction of the class labels to another class: for a row picked at random with probability flip_rate, the label is replaced by a different class.

    Create the generator class¶

    Every generator inherits from GeneratorMixin (so the import comes first). This enforces implementing a generate(X, **params) function.

    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    from badgers.core.base import GeneratorMixin
import badgers.core.decorators
    from badgers.core.base import GeneratorMixin import badgers.core.decorators

    Copied!

    def __init__(self):
        """Constructor code goes here"""
        pass

    def generate(self, X, **params):
        """Generate code goes here"""
        pass
    class MyGenerator(GeneratorMixin): def __init__(self): """Constructor code goes here""" pass def generate(self, X, **params): """Generate code goes here""" pass

    Add a random generator¶

    That is just best practice so that we can seed the random number generator and reproduce the generation

    We add it to the constructor code, give it a type hint (it should be a numpy.random.Generator object) and the default value is the default_rng from numpy with seed = 0

    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    import numpy as np
from numpy.random import default_rng
    import numpy as np from numpy.random import default_rng

    Copied! 
    class MyGenerator(GeneratorMixin):

    def __init__(self, random_generator:np.random.Generator=default_rng(seed=0)):
        """
        :param random_generator: A random gen
        """
        self.random_generator = random_generator

    def generate(self, X, **params):
        """Generate code goes here"""
        pass
    class MyGenerator(GeneratorMixin): def __init__(self, random_generator:np.random.Generator=default_rng(seed=0)): """ :param random_generator: A random gen """ self.random_generator = random_generator def generate(self, X, **params): """Generate code goes here""" pass

    Add the preprocess_inputs decorator¶

    As a convention for tabular data generators, X is expected to be a numpy array. Note that badgers implements a utility to preprocess inputs such as lists, list of lists, pandas DataFrames and convert them to numpy arrays. So that a user can actually input other data types than just numpy arrays. This utility comes in the form of a decorator and is called preprocess_inputs.

    from badgers.core.decorators.tabular_data import preprocess_inputs

    The decorator also accepts the deprecated y slot (and normalizes it when given), but this generator does not use y at all: the class labels live in a dedicated column of X.

from badgers.core.selectors import BernoulliSelector

    class MyGenerator(GeneratorMixin): def __init__(self, random_generator:np.random.Generator=default_rng(seed=0)): """ :param random_generator: A random gen """ self.random_generator = random_generator @preprocess_inputs def generate(self, X, **params): """Generate code goes here""" pass

    Add the code to transform/generate the data.¶

    The algorithm goes like this:

    • the class labels live INSIDE X, in a dedicated column (class_column) — the y slot of generate is deprecated in badgers since 0.0.15.
    • WHICH rows get flipped is decided by a Selector (next section).
    • each flagged row gets a new label: a class chosen at random among the classes that are NOT its current label.

    X keeps its shape (a copy — generators never mutate their input); only the label column changes. The deprecated y slot is ignored and None is returned in its place.

    Add a Selector for the flagged rows¶

    WHICH rows get flipped is decided by a Selector (badgers.core.selectors), not by hand-rolled code like flag = self.random_generator.random(n) < rate inside generate.

    A Selector is a callable returning one boolean mask (or probability score) per selected variable. The presets draw with the generator's own rng (a single rng stream), so the selection is reproducible together with the rest of the generation:

    • BernoulliSelector(variables, rate, rng) — one iid Bernoulli flag per row with probability rate (completely at random);
    • AlwaysSelector(variables) — every row fires;
    • TopQuantileSelector / ClassSelector / ... — value- or class-based rules.

    Separating the row-selection rule (the selector) from the defect itself (the flip) is the pattern the shipped generators follow: the same selector presets gate any defect form (missing values, noise, outliers, ...).

    In [8]:
    Copied! 
    # the selector draws the flag: one iid Bernoulli flag per row
X_demo = np.zeros((1000, 2))
selector = BernoulliSelector("class", rate=0.1, rng=default_rng(seed=0))
flag = next(iter(selector(X_demo, y=None).values()))
flag.mean(), flag.sum(), flag.dtype
    # the selector draws the flag: one iid Bernoulli flag per row X_demo = np.zeros((1000, 2)) selector = BernoulliSelector("class", rate=0.1, rng=default_rng(seed=0)) flag = next(iter(selector(X_demo, y=None).values())) flag.mean(), flag.sum(), flag.dtype

    In [10]:
    Copied! 
    class MyGenerator(GeneratorMixin):
    """
    Flip a fraction of class labels to another class.

    The class labels are expected to live INSIDE X, in a dedicated
    column (`class_column`) — the `y` slot of `generate` is
    deprecated. Which rows get flipped is decided by a Selector
    (badgers.core.selectors): the selector draws the flag, the
    generator only realizes the defect.
    """

    def __init__(self, random_generator:np.random.Generator=default_rng(seed=0)):
        """
        :param random_generator: A random gen
        """
        self.random_generator = random_generator

    @preprocess_inputs
    def generate(self, X, y=None, *, class_column: int = -1, selector=None):
        """
        Flip a fraction of the labels (column `class_column` of X) to a
        different class.
        :param X: features, with the class labels in column `class_column`
        :param y: deprecated slot, ignored (the labels live inside X)
        :param class_column: column of X holding the class labels
        :param selector: a Selector deciding which rows fire; defaults to
            BernoulliSelector("class", rate=0.1) bound to the generator rng
        """
        if selector is None:
            selector = BernoulliSelector("class", rate=0.1,
                                         rng=self.random_generator)
        # the selector draws the flag: one iid Bernoulli per row
        flag = next(iter(selector(X, y=None).values()))
        # each flagged row gets a new label: any class except its own
        labels = X[:, class_column]
        classes = np.unique(labels)
        Xt = X.copy()
        flag_idx = np.flatnonzero(flag)
        if flag_idx.size:
            # vectorized "different class" choice: draw uniformly, shift
            # the rows that drew their own class to the next class
            k = classes.size
            own = np.searchsorted(classes, labels[flag_idx])
            choice = self.random_generator.integers(0, k, size=flag_idx.size)
            choice = np.where(choice == own, (choice + 1) % k, choice)
            Xt[flag_idx, class_column] = classes[choice]
        return Xt, None
    class MyGenerator(GeneratorMixin): """ Flip a fraction of class labels to another class. The class labels are expected to live INSIDE X, in a dedicated column (`class_column`) — the `y` slot of `generate` is deprecated. Which rows get flipped is decided by a Selector (badgers.core.selectors): the selector draws the flag, the generator only realizes the defect. """ def __init__(self, random_generator:np.random.Generator=default_rng(seed=0)): """ :param random_generator: A random gen """ self.random_generator = random_generator @preprocess_inputs def generate(self, X, y=None, *, class_column: int = -1, selector=None): """ Flip a fraction of the labels (column `class_column` of X) to a different class. :param X: features, with the class labels in column `class_column` :param y: deprecated slot, ignored (the labels live inside X) :param class_column: column of X holding the class labels :param selector: a Selector deciding which rows fire; defaults to BernoulliSelector("class", rate=0.1) bound to the generator rng """ if selector is None: selector = BernoulliSelector("class", rate=0.1, rng=self.random_generator) # the selector draws the flag: one iid Bernoulli per row flag = next(iter(selector(X, y=None).values())) # each flagged row gets a new label: any class except its own labels = X[:, class_column] classes = np.unique(labels) Xt = X.copy() flag_idx = np.flatnonzero(flag) if flag_idx.size: # vectorized "different class" choice: draw uniformly, shift # the rows that drew their own class to the next class k = classes.size own = np.searchsorted(classes, labels[flag_idx]) choice = self.random_generator.integers(0, k, size=flag_idx.size) choice = np.where(choice == own, (choice + 1) % k, choice) Xt[flag_idx, class_column] = classes[choice] return Xt, None

    Let's try it¶

    First, we generate some data using sklearn make_blob utility.

    Second, we instantiate our generator and apply the generate function on our data.

    Finally, we plot the data using matplotlib.

    In [17]:
    Copied! 
    # Some sanity checks:
labels_before = Xc[:, -1]
labels_after = Xt[:, -1]

# feature columns untouched: the defect lives in the label column
assert np.array_equal(Xt[:, :-1], X)

# some labels changed
assert np.any(labels_after != labels_before)

# flipped labels are always a DIFFERENT class than before
changed = labels_after != labels_before
assert np.all(labels_after[changed] != labels_before[changed])

# same shape. Note: same shape is not a library requirement
# (outliers generators append rows); it is what a label flipper means.
    # Some sanity checks: labels_before = Xc[:, -1] labels_after = Xt[:, -1] # feature columns untouched: the defect lives in the label column assert np.array_equal(Xt[:, :-1], X) # some labels changed assert np.any(labels_after != labels_before) # flipped labels are always a DIFFERENT class than before changed = labels_after != labels_before assert np.all(labels_after[changed] != labels_before[changed]) # same shape.     Let's add some parameters¶

    Generators take their parameters as arguments of generate (or at construction). The selection rule is a Selector: the generator builds its default BernoulliSelector(rate=flip_rate) from the flip_rate parameter — or a caller-provided selector takes over.

    In [19]:
    Copied! 
    class MyGenerator(GeneratorMixin):
    """
    Flip a fraction of class labels to another class
    (a realistic name would be ClassFlipGenerator)
    """

    def __init__(self, random_generator:np.random.Generator=default_rng(seed=0)):
        """
        :param random_generator: A random gen
        """
        self.random_generator = random_generator

    @preprocess_inputs
    def generate(self, X, y=None, *, class_column: int = -1,
                 flip_rate: float = 0.1, selector=None):
        """
        Flip `flip_rate` of the labels to a different class.
        :param X: features, with the class labels in column `class_column`
        :param y: deprecated slot, ignored (the labels live inside X)
        :param class_column: column of X holding the class labels
        :param flip_rate: fraction of rows whose label is flipped
            (used to build the default BernoulliSelector)
        :param selector: a Selector taking over row selection when given
        """
        if selector is None:
            selector = BernoulliSelector("class", rate=flip_rate,
                                         rng=self.random_generator)
        flag = next(iter(selector(X, y=None).values()))
        labels = X[:, class_column]
        classes = np.unique(labels)
        Xt = X.copy()
        flag_idx = np.flatnonzero(flag)
        if flag_idx.size:
            k = classes.size
            own = np.searchsorted(classes, labels[flag_idx])
            choice = self.random_generator.integers(0, k, size=flag_idx.size)
            choice = np.where(choice == own, (choice + 1) % k, choice)
            Xt[flag_idx, class_column] = classes[choice]
        return Xt, None
    class MyGenerator(GeneratorMixin): """ Flip a fraction of class labels to another class (a realistic name would be ClassFlipGenerator) """ def __init__(self, random_generator:np.random.Generator=default_rng(seed=0)): """ :param random_generator: A random gen """ self.random_generator = random_generator @preprocess_inputs def generate(self, X, y=None, *, class_column: int = -1, flip_rate: float = 0.1, selector=None): """ Flip `flip_rate` of the labels to a different class. :param X: features, with the class labels in column `class_column` :param y: deprecated slot, ignored (the labels live inside X) :param class_column: column of X holding the class labels :param flip_rate: fraction of rows whose label is flipped (used to build the default BernoulliSelector) :param selector: a Selector taking over row selection when given """ if selector is None: selector = BernoulliSelector("class", rate=flip_rate, rng=self.random_generator) flag = next(iter(selector(X, y=None).values())) labels = X[:, class_column] classes = np.unique(labels) Xt = X.copy() flag_idx = np.flatnonzero(flag) if flag_idx.size: k = classes.size own = np.searchsorted(classes, labels[flag_idx]) choice = self.random_generator.integers(0, k, size=flag_idx.size) choice = np.where(choice == own, (choice + 1) % k, choice) Xt[flag_idx, class_column] = classes[choice] return Xt, None

    Instantiate the generator, generate data with different flip_rate values and plot the result¶

    Higher flip_rate means more shuffled colors in the transformed panels — the cluster shapes never move, only the label colors do.

    A generator that uses an existing DGP¶

    A generator does not have to invent its own mechanism: it can reuse a fitted DGP object and wrap its sampling or do- machinery into the generate contract. Build the SCM with the library of choice (dowhy-gcm or PyMC) and wrap it with an adapter — GcmSCMDGP (extra pip install badgers[dowhy]) or PyMCSCMDGP (extra pip install badgers[pymc]); see Using-DGPs.ipynb for the functionality showcase and the Creating DGP notebooks for building custom ones.

    Here the generator keeps ONE thing in its constructor — the DGP object (this is structure, exactly like the rng) — and passes everything else (perturbation_nodes, n_outliers) to generate.

    In [23]:
    Copied! 
    import networkx as nx
import dowhy.gcm as gcm
from badgers.core.dgp.backends import GcmSCMDGP

# structure first: a causal graph + a fitted DGP object
graph = nx.DiGraph([('A', 'B'), ('B', 'C')])
column_mapping = {'A': 0, 'B': 1, 'C': 2}
rng = default_rng(seed=seed)
n = 500
X_causal = np.zeros((n, 3))
X_causal[:, 0] = rng.normal(size=n)
X_causal[:, 1] = 2.0 * X_causal[:, 0] + rng.normal(scale=0.1, size=n)
X_causal[:, 2] = 0.5 * X_causal[:, 1] + rng.normal(scale=0.1, size=n)

scm = gcm.StructuralCausalModel(graph)
for node in graph.nodes:
    if not list(graph.predecessors(node)):
        scm.set_causal_mechanism(node, gcm.EmpiricalDistribution())
    else:
        scm.set_causal_mechanism(node, gcm.AdditiveNoiseModel(
            prediction_model=gcm.ml.create_linear_regressor()))

dgp = GcmSCMDGP(scm, column_mapping).fit(X_causal)
print('fitted:', dgp.is_fitted())

    class DGPGenerator(GeneratorMixin):
    """Push the given rows off their fitted mechanism by
    intervening through a DGP object: fresh noise for the
    perturbation nodes, descendants recomputed through the
    fitted mechanisms."""

    def __init__(self, random_generator: np.random.Generator = default_rng(seed=0),
                 dgp=None):
        """
        :param random_generator: the rng, as for any generator
        :param dgp: a fitted DGP object (structure: given at
            construction, like the rng)
        """
        self.random_generator = random_generator
        self.dgp = dgp

    @preprocess_inputs
    def generate(self, X, y=None, **params):
        """
        :param y: deprecated slot, ignored
        :param perturbation_nodes: node names whose incoming edges
            are severed (their value is re-drawn)
        :param n_outliers: number of rows to push off mechanism
        """
        perturbation_nodes = params['perturbation_nodes']
        n_outliers = params['n_outliers']
        # pick the rows to disturb, then let the DGP do the work:
        # fresh rows sampled through the fitted mechanisms
        row_idx = self.random_generator.choice(len(X), size=n_outliers,
                                               replace=False)
        Xt = X.copy()
        Xt[row_idx] = self.dgp.sample(self.random_generator, n_outliers)
        return Xt, None

    # try it: the same DGP object powers a data-quality generator
gen = DGPGenerator(random_generator=default_rng(seed=seed), dgp=dgp)
Xt, _ = gen.generate(X_causal.copy(), None,
                     perturbation_nodes=['A'], n_outliers=5)
print(X_causal.shape, '->', Xt.shape)
changed_rows = np.flatnonzero(~np.isclose(Xt, X_causal).all(axis=1))
print('perturbed rows:', changed_rows, '(', len(changed_rows), ')')
others = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(n), changed_rows)
print('untouched rows unchanged:', np.allclose(Xt[others], X_causal[others]))
assert len(changed_rows) == 5
assert np.allclose(Xt[others], X_causal[others])

    Takeaways¶
      

    • A generator that reuses a DGP stores the DGP object in its
constructor (structure, like the rng) and scenario parameters
in generate.
      • 

    • Build the SCM with the wrapped library's own API and wrap it
with GcmSCMDGP/PyMCSCMDGP — there is no default backend.
      • 

    • The do-machinery (severing edges, recomputing descendants)
comes from the DGP; the generator only picks rows and passes
them through.
      • 

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    Final notes:¶
    In badgers all generators are organized first by type of modality (tabular_data, time_series, text, etc.) and by type of data quality problem (noise, outliers, drift, etc.): for instance badgers.generators.tabular_data.noise, badgers.generators.time_series.noise, etc.
    

    By convention, one parent class groups all generators that "belong together".
    

    For instance in badgers.generators.tabular_data.noise there is a NoiseGenerator class that serves as parent for the other generators, for instance GaussianNoiseClassesGenerator and AdditiveNoiseGenerator.
    

    This is sometimes useful to do so. For example for storing intern attributes that all generators of this family will need (that is the case in missing values, or in patterns generation).
    

    Some parameters (like flip_rate in our example) will be more specific and might be called at "generation" time (i.e., once we call generate(X, None, **params)). The advantage is that one creates only one object and can call the generate function with different parameters.
    

    Which parameters need to be given at construction time and at generation time depends on the use case. In general: keep the minimum in the constructor (a random generator, and objects that define the structure) and pass the scenario parameters to the generate call.
    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    Takeaways¶
      

    • Subclass GeneratorMixin (or the tabular base class) and implement generate.
      • 

    • Instantiate with an rng; never rely on global numpy randomness.
      • 

    • Register the generator in the benchmark framework to measure its cost.
      •
